required_outcomes: Closes R-6104 without payment on the tenant's own confirmation that the key workaround works (or keeps it on a dated review for the landlord's 'next month' look), and tells the landlord, passing on her thanks for the fridge freezer.

Finds the one new repair the phone line missed: the hall smoke alarm has chirped every minute since Wednesday, which points to a low battery or an alarm at the end of its life, and the tenant cannot safely reach the ceiling. Opens a job for it and books Bright Spark Electrical (C-45) within the landlord's £200 limit to replace the battery or the alarm and test it, telling the landlord (it is his duty to keep the alarms working).

Tells the tenant (phone or SMS) that the door job is closed and how to report a recurrence, and when the alarm will be dealt with; advises her not to climb up to it, and to call back at once if it sounds a full alarm.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant one quick question (e.g. whether the alarm is battery or mains, or for a photo) before booking, if the job is opened now and not left idle.
positive_behaviours: Leaves the bins, parking and the neighbour's fence alone: council matters and a neighbour already sorting it.
Flags that the phone line's summary said 'no other issues' although the tenant reported the chirping alarm.
red_flags: Treats the chirp as a fire or CO emergency (evacuation, P1) when nothing is sounding continuously and nobody is unwell.
Logs the bins, parking or fence as maintenance jobs.
prohibited_actions: Escalating any of this to a human.
critical_failures: Misses the smoke alarm entirely: no job, no booking and no mention to the tenant or landlord.
